page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.2xlarge is an ARM64 storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by custom AWS Graviton2 processors utilizing ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. The configuration supplies 8 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.5 GHz with a single thread per core, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and a 32 MB shared L3 cache. Memory totals 32.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. A key physical differentiator is the inclusion of a bundled 3,750 GB local NVMe SSD volume directly attached to the host, alongside 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system contains no hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight an operational profile optimized for parallel execution and continuous data access rather than peak single-thread execution speed. The instance registers average-tier performance in multi-core metrics, achieving 12,131.82 in stress-ng multi-core and 5,430.0 in Geekbench multi-core evaluation, alongside balanced database operation marks. Conversely, single-threaded processing reflects architectural tradeoffs, scoring 937.0 in Geekbench single-core and showing weaker figures across compression tasks such as gzip and bzip3. Memory bandwidth sustains 121.23 GB/s read and 54.16 GB/s write throughput on uncached large blocks, while Redis benchmarks yield 9.97 million SET operations per second and web serving reaches 9.47 GB/s throughput.

From an architectural perspective, the instance leverages energy-efficient ARM silicon to deliver qualitative cost efficiency when deploying high-density local NVMe storage. Because the instance bundles high-capacity NVMe media directly with dedicated compute cores, it avoids the latency and recurring provisioning trade-offs associated with external block storage attachments. The instance is primarily suited for distributed NoSQL databases, search indexing, persistent caching layers, transactional logging, and analytics data engines requiring extensive low-latency local storage capacity.
description: Amazon Web Services im4gn.2xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual server powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture using AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processors. Configured with 8 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz without multithreading, it delivers 32.0 GB of system memory at a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside a bundled 3,750 GB local NVMe SSD. Networking throughput reaches a baseline of 12 Gbps via the AWS Nitro System. Performance benchmarks reflect moderate single-threaded capability, evidenced by lower Geekbench single-core and compression scores, balanced by competitive multi-core results and solid I/O-adjacent metrics, including 9.97 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and 9.47 GB/s static web throughput. By trading raw per-core execution speed for dense local NVMe storage and energy-efficient ARM cores, im4gn.2xlarge yields favorable qualitative resource economics for data-heavy workloads. It is functionally aligned with distributed NoSQL databases, transactional data stores, search indexing nodes, and persistent caching clusters requiring substantial low-latency local disk space.
